articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document identifies itself as "SJAA EPHEMERIS," the official publication of the San Jose Astronomical Association for November 1993. It specifically notes its volume as 4 and number as 11, serving as the masthead for a club newsletter or journal.

articles.title: The Eyepiece
articles.summary: This newsletter announces upcoming director elections in February and highlights articles on multiple stars and the Vixen 2.4 eyepiece. It details a new portable dobsonian telescope built for the loan program and provides a comprehensive calendar of events for November and December, including star parties and general meetings. The author also solicits member feedback on the preferred future location for club meetings.

articles.title: HOW HIGH IS TOO HIGH? A REVIEW of the Vixen 2.5 mm Eyepiece
articles.summary: This article reviews the Vixen 2.5 mm eyepiece, challenging the common amateur astronomy rule of limiting magnification to '50x per inch of aperture.' The author, Stephen R. Waldee, argues that with high-quality optics and stable atmospheric conditions, much higher magnifications are not only possible but yield exceptional views, citing historical precedents and personal observing experiences. The Vixen eyepiece is highly praised for its superior eye relief, multi-coated lanthanum lenses, and ability to provide clear, detailed high-power views, making it a significant improvement over other high-power oculars.

articles.title: The following table shows our observations of performance of the Vixen 2.5 mm ocular compared to other eyepieces.
articles.summary: This article presents observational performance comparisons of the Vixen 2.5 mm ocular against other eyepieces, sometimes utilizing a Barlow lens to achieve similar magnifications. Observations were conducted on celestial objects such as Vega, Epsilon Lyrae, Saturn, and the Moon, using Meade 80-mm and Celestron 70-mm Fluorite telescopes. The Vixen eyepiece generally demonstrated excellent performance, often producing flawless diffraction patterns and clear images, although its performance varied depending on the target and magnification.

articles.title: DOUBLE, TRIPLE, AND MULTIPLE STARS
articles.summary: This article details the author's recent astronomical observations, focusing on double and multiple star systems, primarily within the constellation Cetus. Despite challenging weather in the UK, the author observed several binaries, including Mira (Omicron Ceti), Gamma Ceti, 84 Ceti, and Sigma 274, providing their characteristics like magnitudes, separations, distances, and periods. The piece also briefly mentions other deep-sky objects and notable stars in the region, offering practical advice for amateur astronomers.

articles.title: Some notes from the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore
articles.summary: The article presents updates from the Space Telescope Science Institute, primarily detailing Comet Shoemaker-Levy (1993e)'s asteroid-like composition, its fragmented state due to Jupiter's gravity, and planned observations for its imminent collision with Jupiter in November 1993. Additionally, it recounts a successful Cub Scout star party held on October 3rd, where despite cloudy conditions, 50 Webelos were able to observe Saturn and other stars.

articles.title: Houge Park Sept 24
articles.summary: This article describes a public star party held at Houge Park on September 24th, attended by many despite some regulars being at Lick Observatory. Participants observed various celestial objects including Saturn, the Moon, M13, M57, and notably Uranus and Neptune, which were a rare treat for public viewing. The sky conditions were decent, and the event was considered a success, lasting until nearly midnight.

articles.title: Introductory Astronomy Class
articles.summary: An introductory astronomy class was held at Houge Park on September 25th at 8 PM, led by Jack Petersen. Several individuals attended, and it's noted that Petersen had previously participated in a Lick Observatory pilgrimage on September 24th, organized by Rick.

articles.title: Locations of SJAA Star Party sites a follow-up
articles.summary: This article, a follow-up to initial site selections by Alice and Dan Finley, details corrected and updated locations for SJAA Star Party sites. The author re-checked and rectified inaccuracies for Houge and Henry Coe parks, also adding an 'old' overflow parking area at Coe and including Fremont Peak for completeness. The author notes that these determinations contain potential errors and assumptions, with an indicated accuracy.

articles.title: SJAA observing sites
articles.summary: This document outlines observing sites for the SJAA, providing geographical coordinates and elevations for various locations in California. It also reports on a tour of Lick Observatory, detailing observations through a 36-inch telescope, and discusses a planned expedition to Bolivia for the 1994 total Solar Eclipse. Additionally, the article reviews an astronomy class covering constellations and presents a calendar of SJAA general meetings, star parties, and observational astronomy classes for 1993-1994.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Status
articles.summary: This article from Paul Barton details the current loaner status of telescopes from the SJAA, listing various instruments, their current users, and due dates, alongside several telescopes currently available for borrowing. It also notes a specialized solar telescope for experienced members, maintains a waiting list for popular models, and provides instructions for members interested in borrowing equipment.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: This document, titled "ASTRO ADS," serves as a classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers to sell or trade astronomically related products and services. It provides contact information for submitting ads, along with several listings for used telescopes, eyepieces, cameras, and offers for skill-sharing or transportation assistance to dark sky sites. Ads typically run for about three months.

articles.title: November 1993
articles.summary: This document provides a table detailing the lunar phases for November 1993. It lists the date and time for the Last Quarter, New Moon, First Quarter, and Full Moon, along with corresponding rise and set times where applicable. The information serves as an astronomical guide for the month.

articles.title: Nearer Planets
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical guide for observing the 'Nearer Planets' (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) during November. It lists key data such as their distance from the Sun (AU), apparent magnitude, and specific observation times likely indicating rise, transit, and set for three dates in the month. Additionally, it includes information on the Sun's coordinates, stellar classification, and astronomical twilight times for dawn and dusk.

articles.title: Sidereal Time
articles.summary: The document provides astronomical timing data, including sidereal time calculations for transit, ascension, and local midnight using PST. It also highlights an upcoming "Darkest Saturday Night" on November 13, detailing sunset, twilight end, and moonset/moonrise times for optimal viewing conditions.

articles.title: TIMES AND DATES ARE PACIFIC DAYLIGHT
articles.summary: This brief note clarifies that all times and dates referenced are in Pacific Daylight Time, though it also mentions 'Local Civil' for time derivation. It credits "Astronomy with Your Personal Computer" by Peter Duffet-Smith and "MacEphem" by Elwood Charles Downey as the sources for these calculations.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors | Ephemeris Contributors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors, including a President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and several Directors, along with their contact phone numbers. It also provides a list of "Ephemeris Contributors" and identifies Bob Madden as the editor, all with contact information.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS
articles.summary: This article provides an update on three comets visible in the sky: Comet Mueller 1993a, Comet Muller 1993p, and Periodic Comet Schwassmann-Wachmann 2 (SW2). SW2 is expected to reach its closest point to the sun on January 23 at 2.07 AU and brighten to approximately magnitude 11 during this visit.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document presents ephemerides for three comets: Comet Mueller (1993a), Comet Mueller (1993p), and Periodic Comet Schwassmann-Wachmann 2. It provides observational data including right ascension, declination, elongation, sky position, and magnitude for each comet, covering dates from October 20 to December 14, 1993.

articles.title: EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: EPHEMERIS is a monthly publication by the San Jose Astronomical Association, which encourages members to submit articles. Submissions should be typed and sent to the editor, Bob Madden, no later than the 12th of the previous month, with text files on 3-1/2" IBM or MAC diskettes being preferred.

articles.title: Membership only: $12 Membership / S&T: $32 Junior (under 18): $20
articles.summary: This document serves as a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), outlining different membership tiers and their respective costs, including options for 'Membership Only', 'Membership/S&T' (Sky & Telescope), and 'Junior' (under 18). It provides instructions for submission via mail or in-person at meetings, payment details, and contact information for the organization.
